note: A SPEC FORM NAMES A VAR, so its argument must be a NAME. `(s/fdef 1 :args)` — a clj-kondo corpus fixture for reader recovery — published a symbol literally called `1`, with a `contains` edge `spec-syntax->1` beside it. A symbol named after a literal is not a var and nothing can ever resolve it, so it is a placeholder identity in a table whose whole contract is that every name in it is referable; the malformed form now falls through to the generic-call branch, which records the spec expression's own call relationships and nothing else. CLJ-D26 also holds here: a keyword spec name is auto-resolved by the reader, so `::email` is published as `:current-ns/email` rather than the literal `::email`, which had left the spec with no resolvable identity any other file could reference. And CLJ-D33 holds here too: the `contains` edge for an annotated var points at its `defn`, not at the `s/fdef`.
